description: Types of renewable energy, technology, global status, and the energy transition

overview.definition: Energy from sources that are naturally replenished on a human timescale
overview.growth: Fastest growing energy source; solar capacity doubled every 3 years since 2010
overview.cost_trends: Solar and wind now cheapest electricity sources ever built in most of world

photovoltaic.principle: Photovoltaic effect; photons knock electrons free in semiconductor (silicon)
photovoltaic.cost: Fell 99% since 1977; ~$0.03/kWh levelized cost in sunny regions

concentrated_solar.principle: Mirrors focus sunlight onto heat transfer fluid → steam → turbine
concentrated_solar.advantage: Can store heat energy; dispatchable power

onshore.turbines: Modern turbines 2–5 MW; blades up to 80 m long

offshore.advantages: Stronger, more consistent winds; less visual impact

wind_energy.global_capacity: ~2.1 TW installed; China, USA, Germany leaders

hydropower.oldest_renewable: Dams and turbines; oldest large-scale renewable electricity
hydropower.advantages: Reliable, dispatchable, long lifespan, pumped-storage stores excess renewable energy
hydropower.disadvantages: Habitat disruption, methane from reservoirs, displacement of communities

largest_plants.three_gorges: 22.5 GW; China; world's largest power station

other_renewables.geothermal: Earth's internal heat; 14 GW; Iceland, USA, Kenya; very low emissions
other_renewables.biomass: Burning organic matter; controversial; deforestation risk vs carbon neutrality
other_renewables.ocean_tidal: Tidal currents and waves; early stage; high resource potential
other_renewables.hydrogen: Green hydrogen from renewable electrolysis; energy storage and fuel for hard-to-decarbonize sectors

energy_storage.need: Solar and wind are variable; storage enables 24/7 clean energy
energy_storage.lithium_ion: Dominant battery technology; EVs and grid storage; cost fell 97% since 1991
energy_storage.pumped_hydro: 95% of global grid storage; pump water uphill; release through turbines
energy_storage.long_duration: Needed for seasonal storage; iron-air, vanadium flow, hydrogen options

energy_transition.iea_net_zero: No new fossil fuel projects needed after 2021; achieve net zero by 2050
energy_transition.investment: $1.7 trillion in clean energy investment in 2023 (first time exceeded fossil fuels)
energy_transition.jobs: Clean energy employs 13.7 million people globally (2023); growing rapidly
